[Documentation](../../docs.html) / [Question types](../../docs.html#question-types)

Add a question, choose Single choice, and give the options the respondent picks 1 from.

![The single-choice question question selected in the editor, its settings outlined.](../../../docs/question-types/single-choice-editor.png){width=100%}

## What the respondent sees

![The question as the respondent sees it.](../../../docs/question-types/single-choice-preview.png){width=90%}

## Settings

- **Answer set.** The options, each with a stored code and the label respondents see.
- **Other, please specify.** Adds a text box for an answer the options miss, kept beside the code.
- **Ordered.** Marks the options as ordered, so the item is analysed as ordinal.

## Best practices for research

Make the options exhaustive and mutually exclusive, or add Other: a respondent with no fitting option guesses.

Reference: Krosnick, J. A., & Presser, S. (2010). Question and questionnaire design. In P. V. Marsden & J. D. Wright (Eds.), *Handbook of survey research* (2nd ed., pp. 263-313). Emerald.
